purpose: Anagrelide is used to lower the number of platelets in your blood when they are too high — a condition called essential thrombocythemia. Having too many platelets can increase your risk of dangerous blood clots or bleeding. This medicine helps bring your platelet count down to a safer level.
how_it_works: Your body makes blood cells in the bone marrow, including platelets, which help your blood clot. Anagrelide works by slowing down the process that creates platelets, so your body makes fewer of them. Think of it as putting the brakes on platelet production without affecting other blood cells too much.
common_side_effects: Headache, dizziness, fast or irregular heartbeat (palpitations), fluid retention or swelling, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, and feeling tired or weak. These are usually mild but let your doctor know if they bother you.
warnings: This medicine can affect your heart, so tell your doctor if you have any heart problems before starting it. It should not be used during pregnancy as it may harm your baby — use reliable birth control while taking it. Regular blood tests and heart monitoring (ECG) will be needed. Avoid grapefruit and tell your pharmacist about all other medicines you take, as interactions are possible.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 0.5 mg taken by mouth twice a day (1 mg total per day). Your doctor will slowly adjust your dose based on your platelet count, usually not going above 10 mg per day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
